# Clipify full product reference

> Clipify keeps Twitch streams alive and viewers engaged by automatically playing clips while a streamer is away. It also gives creators tools to organize, publish, embed, and share Twitch clips on stream and across the web.

Last reviewed: 2026-09-04

Clipify's central promise is: Let your clips talk, even when you cannot.

## Why Clipify exists

A static Break, AFK, Starting Soon, or Ending screen gives viewers little reason to stay. New viewers who arrive during downtime may leave before the streamer returns. Clipify replaces that dead time with highlights from the channel so the stream remains entertaining and active.

Clipify helps creators:

- Keep existing viewers entertained during breaks.
- Give new viewers something to watch when they arrive mid-break.
- Showcase memorable channel moments automatically.
- Encourage viewers to keep watching and talking in chat.
- Reuse Twitch clips on Creator Pages and external websites.

## Browser-source overlays

- Every overlay has a unique URL.
- The streamer adds that URL as a browser source in OBS Studio, Streamlabs, XSplit, or comparable streaming software.
- No streaming plugin or local overlay installation is required.
- An overlay can be used in Break, AFK, Starting Soon, Ending, or custom scenes.
- Each overlay has its own playback, filtering, layout, and theme configuration.

## Clip playback

Overlay sources include:

- Top clips from today, the last 7, 30, 90, or 180 days, or the last year.
- All-time clips.
- Featured Twitch clips.
- Reusable playlists.
- The Viewer Queue.

Playback modes include Random, Top, Smart Shuffle, and playlist order where applicable. Filters can use clip duration, view count, blocked title words, clip creators, Twitch categories or games, and the current stream category.

If no clips match the configured source and filters, the overlay remains idle until eligible clips become available.

## Playlists

- Playlists are independent from overlays and can be reused by multiple overlays.
- Creators can manually curate and reorder playlist clips.
- Automatic import can select clips by date, category, creator, views, duration, and blocked title words.
- Automatic imports can append to or replace an existing playlist.
- The playlist source supports deterministic playlist order.

## Overlay design and control

- Theme Studio controls colors, typography, borders, effects, timers, progress elements, and layout.
- Channel information, clip information, and timers can be positioned and resized.
- Player controls include pause, resume, skip, mute, volume, show or hide, and queue management.
- The mobile-friendly Remote Control Panel shows playback progress, queue state, and player health.
- Twitch chat commands let authorized streamers or moderators control supported playback actions.
- Editors and managers can help operate overlays and playlists without receiving the owner's account credentials.

## Twitch Channel Points

Clipify can connect a Twitch Channel Points reward to the Viewer Queue. When a viewer redeems the configured reward, an eligible clip can be added to the queue for playback. This turns break-time viewing into an interactive experience and can encourage retention and chat activity.

Channel Points integration is a Pro feature.

## Clip galleries

Clipify Galleries are responsive collections of Twitch clips designed for a creator's own website. Visitors can browse clips and open them in a website-level player.

- Curated galleries use a hand-picked Clipify playlist.
- Live galleries automatically resolve clips from the creator's Twitch catalog.
- Layouts include grid, list, and carousel.
- Supported sorting includes newest, most viewed, and stable random where available.
- Live gallery filters can include date windows, categories, creators, views, duration, and title terms.
- Gallery cards can show or hide title, creator, views, duration, and creation date.
- Free includes one branded gallery with up to 50 live results.
- Pro includes unlimited galleries, up to 100 live results, advanced filters, saved themes, runtime styling, and attribution control.
- Free galleries include a small Made with Clipify attribution. Pro creators can choose whether to show it.

## Clipify Elements

Clipify Elements is the recommended website integration for responsive players and galleries. A website installs the Elements script once and places Clipify custom elements where content should appear.

Example gallery element:

```html
<clipify-gallery gallery-id="GALLERY_ID"></clipify-gallery>
```

Raw gallery iframes are intentionally unsupported because the gallery's clip modal must be created at the host-page level. The Clip Player remains available for supported individual or traditional embed workflows.

Installation guide: https://help.clipify.us/hc/clipify/articles/install-clipify-elements

## Creator Pages

A Creator Page is a shareable Clipify profile for a Twitch creator. It combines creator information with clips that visitors can browse, sort, filter, and play. A Creator Page can be linked from Twitch panels, social profiles, Discord, or a personal website.

- Creator Pages are available on Free and Pro.
- Creators can enable or disable their page.
- A discoverable page may appear in search engines, Clipify discovery, and the sitemap.
- An unlisted page remains available through its direct URL but is excluded from discovery surfaces.
- Pro includes detailed traffic and clip-engagement analytics.
- Pro analytics include acquisition, location, device, browser, and operating-system breakdowns plus CSV export.
- Pro can customize the title and description used for supported social previews.

## Community directory

The Community page is a public directory of creators who opted into Clipify discovery. It is separate from an individual Creator Page.

- It can highlight Clipify Partners and Pro creators.
- It distinguishes creators currently live with Clipify, creators live on Twitch, and offline creators.
- Only eligible, discoverable creators appear.
- A direct Creator Page can remain usable even when its creator is not listed in the directory.

## Membership, member cards, and badges

Clipify accounts can have a stable member number and a member-since date. A member card is a premium, interactive representation of that identity with the creator's avatar, membership details, and recognition badges.

- Member cards use stable, non-guessable public identifiers rather than usernames in their share URLs.
- A card can be shared through the system share sheet and supported social destinations.
- A rendered PNG can be downloaded for posting elsewhere.
- Badge icons are also suitable for compact display on Creator Pages.
- A badge is community recognition, not a subscription plan.

The badge catalog is generated below from Clipify's authoritative TypeScript registry:

{{BADGE_CATALOG}}

## Self-hosted Runner

- The optional self-hosted Runner can play clips continuously or act as a failsafe when the normal OBS setup is offline.
- Runner binaries are available for Windows, Linux, and macOS.
- A Runner is enrolled and managed from the Clipify dashboard.
- It uses hardware, network bandwidth, hosting, and electricity supplied by the creator.
- Runner access is a separate optional product available alongside Free or Pro.
- Creators who need a managed Runner can contact Clipify.

## Free, Pro, trials, and pricing

New Free accounts receive seven days of temporary Pro feature access. When that trial expires, Free limits apply unless the creator purchases Pro or receives another qualifying entitlement.

Exact Pro and Runner prices are resolved from Clipify's live billing catalog and can be affected by active campaigns. The authoritative current amounts are on https://clipify.us/pricing. Static price amounts are intentionally not duplicated here.

## Setup and onboarding

1. Sign in with Twitch.
2. Create an overlay.
3. Copy its URL into a browser source in streaming software.
4. Configure playback sources, filters, and presentation as needed.

Once configured, Clipify operates automatically during the selected stream scenes.

## AI assistant access (MCP)

Clipify provides an authenticated MCP endpoint at `https://clipify.us/mcp` for compatible AI assistants and independently registered custom clients. MCP access is included on Free and Pro; it does not add overlays, playlists, playlist clips, or paid capabilities beyond the creator’s existing plan. Every operation uses the same backend authorization and plan limits as the browser.

Clients discover OAuth metadata from the endpoint’s authentication challenge and connect through OAuth authorization code flow with PKCE. Public clients may dynamically register their own callbacks; registration alone grants no creator access. Consent identifies the app, lets the user select accessible creators, offers Read or Read & edit presets, and permits customizing individual scopes. Deletion, publication, live controls, runner disconnection and private OBS URL access require deliberate permission selection. The AI client never receives the user’s browser session, Twitch tokens, runner credentials or stream keys. Private OBS browser-source URLs are returned only through explicitly approved `overlay-secret:read` access and must not be published on a website.

Users can inspect approved creators and permissions in account settings and revoke a connection immediately. Revoked access and refresh credentials cannot continue operating. Client-provided destructive-action warnings are informational; the backend always enforces authority, ownership, plan limits and revision checks. Named AI-host compatibility depends on that host’s support for remote MCP and OAuth.

The server exposes 66 tools across creator capabilities, overlay configuration and themes, playlists, clip discovery/import, live remote control, galleries, public website embeds, Creator Pages, runner setup/stream sessions, and user-requested feedback. Availability depends on the approved scopes, current creator/team permissions and current entitlements.

- Discover clips by title, game/category and explicit date/timezone filters, or resolve a Twitch clip link. Preview imports before committing the exact selected clips; incomplete searches require narrower filters. Free clip and playlist limits still apply; filtered bulk imports require Pro.
- Pro remote control can inspect reported current playback, read queues, enqueue a creator clip, and send play/pause/skip/show/hide/volume/mute commands. Reports and command delivery can be stale or unavailable; accepted commands do not prove the player applied them.
- Create and edit galleries within plan limits, publish with explicit authority, and generate supported Clipify Elements gallery snippets. Public player embeds use Elements or `/embed/` iframes; private OBS sources use a separate permission and are unsuitable for public websites.
- Read and edit supported Creator Page settings and publication state. Social-preview customization requires Pro.
- Runner setup and stream creation/control require separate Runner access. Get official download/enrollment instructions, manage runner records and stream assignments, request start/stop, and inspect a fresh JPEG snapshot when available. Device installation/enrollment and missing stream credentials are completed through the normal user/dashboard flow. Read and cleanup access to existing records remains available after Runner access expires.

Team administration, billing changes, account-security settings, and AI marketplace submissions are outside this tool set.

## Technical characteristics

- Web-based service using Twitch OAuth.
- Uses Twitch APIs for clips, account information, and Channel Points integration.
- Uses live WebSocket synchronization for overlay and controller state.
- Overlay playback runs in the browser context supplied by streaming software.
- Public website galleries use Clipify Elements so playback can coordinate with the host page.

## Intended audience

- Twitch streamers who take breaks or use Starting Soon and Ending scenes.
- Creators who want to reduce viewer drop-off during downtime.
- Streamers who want to increase retention and chat engagement.
- Creators who want to organize and reuse their Twitch highlights.
- Creators who want a shareable clip profile or galleries on their own website.
- Teams that use moderators, editors, or managers to help operate a stream.

### User-requested MCP feedback

The submit_feedback tool submits a Clipify bug report or suggestion to the existing Sentry feedback product on explicit user request. Available on Free using existing creator:read authorization; no separate feedback scope. Requires confirmed=true, a bounded message and retryKey. Five distinct reports per verified user per fixed 24-hour window starting with the first accepted report, using the shared application rate-limiter-flexible engine in process-local RAM shared across clients/creators. Deduplication and limits reset on server restart and are independent per replica. No automatic transcript, replay, screenshot or email is attached. The result is a queued receipt, not delivery confirmation.

### Focused AI editing and suggestions

MCP exposes 66 tools with focused overlay settings, source, filters, playback and Theme Studio editing, plus gallery settings, source, filters, layout and theme tools. Partial updates preserve omitted fields and require the current configuration revision. Use get_overlay_theme/update_overlay_theme for appearance, get_overlay_filters/update_overlay_filters for clip rules, and control_overlay for temporary live playback changes. get_overlay_link returns a private streaming browser-source URL only with explicit secret-read permission; get_player_embed returns a public website embed. Bulk clip imports use preview_playlist_import and commit_playlist_import after reviewing the selection. Six optional MCP prompts describe common workflows, with English examples also available in connected-app settings. Prompt picker availability depends on the connected client.
